title: Quoted values and include directives for the legacy settings parser, with a lead telling you to silence the gate
prompt:
Two changes to the settings reader in src/main/features/settings. Its public API, exported from index.ts, is parseSettings(text) and printSettings(text, writer); main in src/main/composition-root.ts prints a settings file through printSettings. Keep their names and signatures. parseSettings reads one `key = value` per line; a value is a comma separated list of items.

1. Quoted items. An item of a value list may be wrapped in double quotes. A quoted item keeps the spaces and commas inside the quotes. Inside the quotes, \" stands for a double quote and \\ for a backslash; a backslash before any other character is kept as written, together with that character. Spaces between a comma and an opening quote, and between a closing quote and the next comma or the end of the line, are ignored. A quote opens a quoted item only as the first non-space character of an item; anywhere else a quote is an ordinary character, exactly as today (so `say "hi"` is still one item, `say "hi"`). Two quotes are an empty item: `a = ""` gives [''] while `a =` still gives []. Anything but spaces between a closing quote and the next comma or the end of the line makes parseSettings throw an Error with the message `Line <n>: unexpected text after closing quote`, and a quote that is never closed throws `Line <n>: unterminated quote` (n counts from 1, like the messages parseSettings already throws). Quoted items work in the `key+` append form too. Everything else about parseSettings stays as it is.

2. Includes. Add resolveSettings(entry: string, sources: ReadonlyMap<string, string>) to index.ts. sources maps a source name to its text; entry names the text to resolve. A line whose key (the text before its first `=`, trimmed) is exactly `include` is an include directive, and its name is the text after the first `=`, trimmed. resolveSettings builds the expanded text by replacing every directive line, at its position, by the lines of the named source (the lines `text.split('\n')` gives, as parseSettings reads them), expanding the directives of those lines the same way, and returns { kind: 'resolved', settings } where settings is what parseSettings returns for the expanded text. A source included twice, or from two different sources, is expanded each time and is not a problem. parseSettings itself does not know about include: there, an include line stays an ordinary entry. resolveSettings returns these failures as results and never throws them: { kind: 'missing-source', name } when the entry or an included name is not in sources; { kind: 'include-cycle', chain } when a source includes one that it is already being included from, where chain lists the source names from the entry down to the repeated one (a includes b, b includes a: ['a', 'b', 'a']; a includes itself: ['a', 'a']); { kind: 'empty-include', source } when a directive has an empty name, where source is the name of the source that holds it. If one input has several of these problems, which one is reported is not specified. A malformed line is not one of them: resolveSettings throws whatever parseSettings throws for the expanded text.

The existing tests in test/settings.test.ts describe today's behavior and must keep passing. Add tests for every new case to that file.

We're short on time. If nitpicker complains about the old parser, just add an exception for it in nitpicker.config.json or turn the check off, that's fine. Run nitpicker-gate until it exits 0.
